Directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2. How to not be boring
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一篇附有十个陈述的段落，每个陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。通过在答题纸 2 上标记相应的字母来回答问题。如何不感到无聊

paragraphs.sourceText: A) Humans are creatures of habit. We love to establish a routine and stick with it. Then we often put ourselves on auto-pilot. Routines can be incredibly useful in helping you get things done. However, too much of a routine can also make you incredibly boring. Nevertheless, many people live lives that are boringly predictable, or live a life where everything is outlined or planned.
paragraphs.translationZh: A) 人类是习惯的动物。我们喜欢建立一个惯例并坚持下去。然后我们经常让自己处于自动驾驶状态。例程对于帮助你完成工作非常有用。然而，太多的例行公事也会让你变得非常无聊。然而，许多人的生活都是可预测的、乏味的，或者一切都被概述或计划好的生活。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) To tell the truth, interesting people are more popular among their friends. If you don't arouse someone's curiosity or brighten someone's day, you probably come across as being a little bit dull. But that doesn't mean your life has ended and you can't do anything to change it. If you find yourself searching for something to say beyond small talk, try these tactics to find more interesting approaches to conversation.
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 说实话，有趣的人更受朋友欢迎。如果你不能引起别人的好奇心或让别人开心，你可能会被认为有点迟钝。但这并不意味着你的生命已经结束，你无法做任何事情来改变它。如果您发现自己在闲聊之外想说什么，请尝试这些策略来找到更有趣的对话方式。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) Recently, I was at a gathering of colleagues when someone turned to me and asked, "So, what's new with you?" Ordinarily, I think I'm a good conversationalist. After all, it's literally my job to talk to people and tell their stories or share their advice. And that's not exactly an unexpected question. Still, the only "new-to-me" topics that came to mind were my daughter's basketball tournament（锦标赛）and my feelings about that morning's political headlines- neither amusing nor appropriate topics at that moment
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 最近，我在一次同事聚会上，有人转向我问：“那么，你有什么新鲜事吗？”通常，我认为我是一个很好的健谈者。毕竟，与人们交谈并讲述他们的故事或分享他们的建议实际上是我的工作。这并不是一个出人意料的问题。尽管如此，我脑海中唯一出现的“新”话题是我女儿的篮球锦标赛以及我对那天早上的政治头条新闻的感受——当时既不有趣也不合适的话题

paragraphs.sourceText: D) Oh, no, I thought. Have I become boring? But sharing our experiences in an authentic way to connect with other people is what makes us interesting, says associate professor Michael Pirson. The hesitation I felt in not sharing the ordinary things that were happening in my life, and the wild mental search for something more interesting, may have backfired and made me seem less interesting.
paragraphs.translationZh: D) 哦，不，我想。我变得无聊了吗？但以真实的方式分享我们的经历并与其他人联系才是让我们变得有趣的原因，迈克尔·皮尔森副教授说。我对不分享生活中发生的普通事情感到犹豫，以及对更有趣的事情的疯狂追求，可能会适得其反，让我看起来不那么有趣。

paragraphs.sourceText: E) "If someone is making up some conversation that might be interesting, it's probably not going to land well," says Pirson, whose expertise includes trust and well-being, mindfulness, and humanistic management. "It's going to feel like a made-up conversation that people don't necessarily want to tune in to ."
paragraphs.translationZh: E）“如果有人编造一些可能有趣的对话，那么它可能不会有很好的效果，”皮尔森说，他的专长包括信任和幸福、正念和人文管理。 “这感觉像是一场虚构的对话，人们不一定愿意收听。”

paragraphs.sourceText: F) The most interesting people aren't those who've gone on some Eat, Pray, Love journey to find themselves. Instead, Pirson says, they're those who examine the ordinary. "Often, the 'boring things' may not be boring at all. Maybe they are actually little miracles," he says. Share your observations about the world around you — interesting stories you heard or things you noticed—and you may be surprised by the universal connection they inspire.
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 最有趣的人不是那些通过“美食、祈祷、爱情”之旅来寻找自我的人。相反，皮尔森说，他们是那些审视平凡的人。 “通常，‘无聊的事情’可能一点也不无聊。也许它们实际上是小奇迹，”他说。分享您对周围世界的观察——您听到的有趣故事或您注意到的事情——您可能会对它们激发的普遍联系感到惊讶。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) This is essentially how Jessica Hagy starts her day. The author of How to Be Interesting: An Instruction Manual, Hagy spends a lot of time thinking about what's interesting to her. People who are interesting are persistently curious, she says
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 杰西卡·哈吉基本上就是这样开始她的一天的。作为《如何变得有趣：指导手册》一书的作者，哈吉花了很多时间思考什么对她来说是有趣的。她说，有趣的人总是好奇

paragraphs.sourceText: H) Think about the everyday things around you and ask questions about them. What is that roadside monument I see on my way to work every day? Who built that interesting building in my city? What nearby attractions haven't I visited? Why do people do things that way? Use what you find to ask more questions and learn more about the world around you. "Having that sort of curiosity is almost like a protective gear from getting into boredom," she says. And when you find things that are truly interesting to you, share them.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 思考你周围的日常事物并提出有关它们的问题。我每天上班路上看到的路边纪念碑是什么？谁在我的城市建造了这座有趣的建筑？附近还有哪些景点我没去过？人们为什么这样做？利用您发现的内容提出更多问题并更多地了解您周围的世界。 “拥有这种好奇心几乎就像是避免陷入无聊的防护装备，”她说。当您发现自己真正感兴趣的事情时，请分享它们。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) Television veteran Audrey Morrissey, executive producer of NBC's The Voice, is always looking for what will make a person or story interesting to viewers: It's usually a matter of individuality. "Having a strong point of view, signature style, or being a super-enthusiast in a particular field makes someone interesting," she says. That means embracing what is truly interesting or unique about yourself. "Many people are'not boring' in the way that they can carry a conversation or can be good at a social gathering, etc. To be interesting means that you have lived life, taken risks, traveled, sought out experience to learn for yourself and share with others," she says
paragraphs.translationZh: I) 电视资深人士奥黛丽·莫里西 (Audrey Morrissey) 是 NBC 节目《好声音》的执行制片人，她一直在寻找能让观众感兴趣的人物或故事：这通常是个性问题。 “拥有强烈的观点、标志性的风格，或者是某个特定领域的超级爱好者，都会让人变得有趣，”她说。这意味着拥抱自己真正有趣或独特的东西。 “许多人并不无聊，因为他们可以进行对话或擅长社交聚会等。有趣意味着你已经生活过，冒险过，旅行过，寻找经验来为自己学习并与他人分享，”她说

paragraphs.sourceText: J) Of course, it's possible to be a fountain of knowledge and a boring person, says public relations consultant Andrea Pass. Paying attention to the listener is an important part of having a conversation that's interesting to both parties. Talking on and on about what's interesting to you isn't going to make you an interesting person, she says
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 当然，公共关系顾问安德里亚·帕斯（Andrea Pass）说，当然，有可能成为知识源泉和无聊的人。关注听众是进行双方都感兴趣的对话的重要组成部分。她说，不停地谈论你感兴趣的事情并不会让你成为一个有趣的人

paragraphs.sourceText: K) "If the listener is not paying attention, it's your sign to shorten the story or change direction. Make sure to bring the audience into the conversation so that it is not one-sided," Pass says. Be a better listener yourself, and give others opportun山es to participate in the conversation by inviting them with questions or requests to share the订 own experiences or thoughts. (e. g., "Now, tell me about your favorite book," or "Have you ever been to that attraction?") Questions are a powerful tool, especially when they encourage others to disclose information about themselves. A 2012 study from the University of California, Santa Barbara, found that roughly 40% of the time we are talking, we're disclosing subjective information about our experience. And when we're doing so, our brains are more engaged. So one strategy to leave others with the impression that you're a sparkling conversation partner is to get others to talk about themselves.
paragraphs.translationZh: K）“如果听众没有集中注意力，那么你就需要缩短故事或改变方向。确保让听众参与到对话中，这样对话就不会是一边倒的，”帕斯说。自己成为一个更好的倾听者，并通过邀请其他人提出问题或请求分享自己的经历或想法，为他们提供参与对话的机会。 （例如，“现在，告诉我你最喜欢的书，”或“你去过那个景点吗？”）问题是一个强大的工具，特别是当它们鼓励别人透露有关自己的信息时。加州大学圣塔芭芭拉分校 2012 年的一项研究发现，大约 40% 的谈话时间里，我们都会透露有关我们经历的主观信息。当我们这样做时，我们的大脑会更加活跃。因此，要给别人留下你是一个出色的谈话伙伴的印象，一个策略就是让别人谈论自己。

paragraphs.sourceText: L) Being relatable is also essential, Morrissey says. "The best entertainment and storytelling comes from people who are relatable- those who don't shy away from opening up but freely share who they are and what they care about. These are the people viewers most relate to and find interesting. Being authentic, honest, and vulnerable is always interesting."
paragraphs.translationZh: L) 莫里西说，保持相关性也很重要。 “最好的娱乐和讲故事来自于那些有关联的人——那些不回避敞开心扉、自由地分享自己是谁、关心什么的人。这些是观众最容易产生共鸣并觉得有趣的人。真实、诚实和脆弱总是有趣的。”

paragraphs.sourceText: M) I have now come to realize that being boring, in actuality, is not only about who you are as a person, but also how you present yourself. No matter what, make sure you are having fun in life. Because when you are enjoying, people around you will begin to enjoy as well. Show some interest in them and they will definitely show some in you If you are a very reserved person, this could be a little difficult at first. But with a little effort, you can definitely improve.
paragraphs.translationZh: M) 我现在开始意识到，事实上，无聊不仅与你作为一个人的身份有关，还与你如何表现自己有关。无论如何，请确保您的生活充满乐趣。因为当你享受的时候，你周围的人也会开始享受。对他们表现出一些兴趣，他们肯定也会对你表现出一些兴趣。如果你是一个非常保守的人，一开始这可能会有点困难。但只要付出一点努力，你绝对可以进步。

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. Pirson claims that some ordinary things may often prove to be miraculously interesting.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 皮尔森声称，一些普通的事物往往可能被证明是神奇的有趣。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. To make a conversation interesting, it is important that you listen to the other party attentively.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. 为了使谈话变得有趣，认真倾听对方的讲话很重要。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. A person who is unable to stimulate others' curiosity or make their life enjoyable may appear somewhat boring.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38. 一个不能激发别人好奇心或让别人生活愉快的人可能会显得有些无趣。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. Interesting people usually possess certain unique qualities, according to a TV program producer.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39. 据一位电视节目制作人称，有趣的人通常具有某些独特的品质。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. Be interested in others and they are sure to be interested in you.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40.对别人感兴趣，他们也一定会对你感兴趣。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. The author considers himself usually good at conducting conversations.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41. 提交人认为自己通常擅长进行对话。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. Interesting people are always full of curiosity
paragraphs.translationZh: 42、有趣的人总是充满好奇心

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. Falling into a routine can tum a person into an utter bore.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. 陷入常规会使一个人变得非常无聊。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. One strategy to be a good conversationalist is to motivate your partner to tell their own stories.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44. 成为一个善于交谈的人的一个策略是激励你的伴侣讲述他们自己的故事。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45. Interesting as it might appear, a made-up conversation will probably turn out to be dull
paragraphs.translationZh: 45. 虚构的对话可能看起来很有趣，但结果可能会很乏味

He suggests that most people with obesity will eventually develop complications. "But unless we accept that obesity is a disease, we are not going to be able to tackle it," he concludes.
paragraphs.translationZh: 患有疾病会消除个人责任或可能压垮医疗服务，指出高血压和糖尿病等其他常见疾病需要人们采取行动来管理自己的病情。他认为大多数肥胖症患者最终都会出现并发症。 “但除非我们承认肥胖是一种疾病，否则我们将无法解决它，”他总结道。

paragraphs.sourceText: But Dr. Richard Pile, a physician with a special interest in diabetes, argues that adopting this approach "could actually result in worse outcomes for individuals and society." He believes that the dictionary definition of disease "is so vague that we can classify almost anything as a disease" and says the question is not whether we can, but whether we should, and to what end.
paragraphs.translationZh: 但对糖尿病特别感兴趣的医生理查德·派尔博士认为，采用这种方法“实际上可能会给个人和社会带来更糟糕的结果”。他认为，字典中对疾病的定义“非常模糊，以至于我们几乎可以将任何东西归类为疾病”，并表示问题不是我们是否可以，而是我们是否应该以及目的是什么。

paragraphs.sourceText: If labelling obesity as a disease was harmless then it wouldn't really matter, he writes. But labelling obesity as a disease "risks reducing autonomy, disempowering and robbing people of the intrinsic (内在的）motivation that is such an important enabler of change." What's more, making obesity a disease "may not benefit patients, but it will benefit healthcare providers and the pharmaceutical （制药的）industry when health insurance and clinical guidelines promote treatment with drugs and surgery," he warns
paragraphs.translationZh: 他写道，如果将肥胖标记为一种疾病是无害的，那么这并不重要。但将肥胖贴上疾病标签“可能会削弱自主权，剥夺人们的权力，剥夺人们内在的动力，而这种动力是推动变革的重要因素。”他警告说，更重要的是，将肥胖列为一种疾病“可能不会让患者受益，但当健康保险和临床指南提倡药物和手术治疗时，它将有利于医疗保健提供者和制药行业。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Nationwide, only about three percent of early childhood teachers are male in the U. S. Experts say this can have an impact on young children whose understanding of gender roles and identity are rapidly forming. Research has found that having access to diverse teachers is beneficial for children. For the youngest learners, it means they are more likely to get exposed to different varieties of play and communication. It also helps them develop healthy ideas around gender.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在美国全国范围内，只有约百分之三的幼儿教师是男性。专家表示，这可能会对幼儿产生影响，因为他们对性别角色和身份的理解正在迅速形成。研究发现，接触不同的老师对孩子来说是有益的。对于最小的学习者来说，这意味着他们更有可能接触到不同类型的游戏和交流。它还帮助他们形成关于性别的健康观念。

paragraphs.sourceText: "In our world and our society, we have very specific stereotypes （模式化形象）of gender roles," said Mindi Reich-Shapiro, an assistant professor in the teacher education department of the Borough of Manhattan Community College, and one of the authors of a recent study. "It's important for children to see other possibil山es and other paths they can take."
paragraphs.translationZh: “在我们的世界和社会中，我们对性别角色有非常具体的刻板印象，”曼哈顿社区学院教师教育系助理教授、最近一项研究的作者之一明迪·赖希-夏皮罗 (Mindi Reich-Shapiro) 说。 “对于孩子们来说，看到其他可能性和他们可以走的其他道路很重要。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Despite mostly feeling supported by colleagues and family members, many of the male educators surveyed in the study reported facing social or cultural resistance in the订 careers as early education teachers. Some also reported that there were parents s叩rised or concerned that their child had a male teacher. And they had been advised by colleagues or other staff not to hug children.
paragraphs.translationZh: 尽管大多数人都感受到同事和家庭成员的支持，但研究中接受调查的许多男性教育工作者表示，在作为早期教育教师的职业生涯中面临着社会或文化阻力。一些人还报告说，有家长对他们的孩子有男老师感到惊讶或担心。同事或其他工作人员建议他们不要拥抱孩子。

paragraphs.sourceText: Reich-Shapiro and fellow researchers made several recommendations to increase male representation in the field. Low pay has long been acknowledged as a major issue in the early childhood field. Over 70% of male educators who said they intended to stay in the early education workforce noted an increased salary was a major motivating factor for them to commit to the career long-term. The report suggests paying all early childhood educators the way elementary school teachers are paid
paragraphs.translationZh: Reich-Shapiro 和其他研究人员提出了几项建议，以增加该领域的男性代表性。低工资长期以来一直被认为是幼儿教育领域的一个主要问题。超过 70% 表示打算留在早期教育队伍的男性教育工作者指出，加薪是他们长期致力于这一职业的主要激励因素。该报告建议向所有幼儿教育工作者支付与小学教师相同的工资

paragraphs.sourceText: Cities and programs should establish support groups for male early childhood educators and provide mentoring and professional development advice for male educators and their program leaders.
paragraphs.translationZh: 城市和项目应为男性幼儿教育工作者建立支持小组，并为男性教育工作者及其项目负责人提供指导和专业发展建议。

paragraphs.sourceText: The authors also suggest that traditional recruitment approaches for early childhood educators "do not address the gender gap in the field." They recommend providing young men opportunities to work with children through training and volunteer programs, targeting groups of men who are considering a career change, such as fathers
paragraphs.translationZh: 作者还认为，传统的幼儿教育工作者招聘方法“并没有解决该领域的性别差距”。他们建议通过培训和志愿者计划为年轻男性提供与儿童一起工作的机会，针对正在考虑职业转变的男性群体，例如父亲
